subject: Meteorology
title: Mountain Waves
description: A quick win: understand Mountain Waves.

hook.text: When stable air flows over mountains, it can create invisible waves downstream—dangerous oscillations for aircraft.

buildup.text: Mountain waves can extend to the stratosphere—with vertical air currents strong enough to exceed climb capability.

discovery.text: Lenticular clouds mark the crests of mountain waves—smooth, lens-shaped formations that signal the wave's presence.

twist.text: Rotor zones below the wave crests contain violent, tumbling turbulence—some of the most dangerous in aviation.

climax.text: A BOAC airliner broke apart in severe mountain wave turbulence near Mt. Fuji in 1966—killing all 124 aboard.

punchline.text: Smooth clouds, violent air—mountains create invisible traps.

quiz.question: What cloud type signals the presence of mountain waves?
